t.3.54.1: Thus addressed, Vaidehī, fearless though worn down by grief, placed a blade of grass between them and replied to Rāvaṇa.
t.3.54.2: There is a king named Daśaratha, unshakable like a dam of dharma, true to his word and widely renowned; that Rāghava is his son.
t.3.54.3: He who is named Rāma, righteous of soul, renowned throughout the three worlds, long-armed and large-eyed, he is my husband, he is my god.
t.3.54.4: Born in the family of the Ikṣvākus, lion-shouldered and of great splendour, he, together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, will take away your life.
t.3.54.6: These rākṣasas who have been described, terrible in form and of great strength, all become venomless before Rāghava, just as serpents do before Suparṇa.
t.3.54.5: If I had been assaulted by you by force before his very eyes, you would now lie slain in battle, as Khara lies in Janasthāna.
t.3.54.7: Those gold-adorned arrows of his, loosed from the bowstring, will shatter your body as the waves wear away the bank of the Gaṅgā.
t.3.54.9: That mighty Rāghava will bring an end to you, whose life is all but spent; like a beast of sacrifice bound to the post, you will hardly keep your life.
t.3.54.8: Even if you cannot be slain by asuras or by suras, O Rāvaṇa, having stirred up this very great enmity, you will not escape him alive.
t.3.54.10: If that Rāma were to look upon you with an eye blazing with fury, O demon, you would this very day be burnt up and would instantly meet your ruin.
t.3.54.11: He who could hurl the moon from the sky down to the earth or destroy it, or who could even dry up the ocean, he alone could free Sītā from here.
t.3.54.12: Your life is spent, your fortune gone, your strength gone, your senses gone; through your own deed, Laṅkā will be joined with widowhood.
t.3.54.13: This sinful deed of yours will not bring you a happy outcome, for I have been carried off by you against my will, from my husband's side and from the forest.
t.3.54.14: For he, my husband, endowed with divine power and of great splendor, fearless and relying on his own valor, dwells in the desolate Daṇḍaka forest.
t.3.54.15: In battle he will drive out from your limbs, with a shower of arrows, your pride, your strength, your valour, and such arrogance as yours.
t.3.54.16: When the destruction of beings, driven on by Time, comes into view, then men who have fallen under the sway of Time grow heedless in what they ought to do.
t.3.54.17: O vilest of rākṣasas, by assaulting me you have brought upon yourself this hour of yours, the time for the destruction of yourself, of the rākṣasas, and of your inner palace.
t.3.54.18: The sacrificial altar standing in the midst of the sacrifice, adorned with ladles and vessels and purified by the mantras of the twice-born, cannot be trampled upon by a caṇḍāla.
t.3.54.20: Having thus spoken these very harsh words out of anger, Vaidehī, the princess of Mithilā, said nothing further to Rāvaṇa there.
t.3.54.19: Bind this senseless body or have it slain, O Rākṣasa; this body is not to be preserved by me, nor even my life. For I shall never be able to bring reproach upon myself on earth.
t.3.54.21: Having heard Sītā's harsh words, which made the hair stand on end, he then replied to Sītā with words meant to show her terror.
t.3.54.22: Hear my words, O Maithilī, O passionate lady: if within this time of twelve months you do not come to me, O sweetly smiling one, then the cooks will cut you into pieces for my morning meal.
t.3.54.23: Having spoken these harsh words, Rāvaṇa, who makes his enemies cry out, then, enraged, spoke these words to the rākṣasīs.
t.3.54.25: At his very word, those misshapen women of dreadful appearance, having joined their palms in reverence, surrounded Maithilī.
t.3.54.24: Swiftly, then, O rākṣasīs, misshapen and terrible to behold, eaters of flesh and blood, you shall break this woman's pride.
t.3.54.26: Then King Rāvaṇa, terrible to behold, spoke to them, making the earth quake with the stamping of his feet as though he were splitting it apart.
t.3.54.27: "Let Maithilī be led into the midst of the Aśoka grove," he said. "There let her be guarded secretly, surrounded by you."
t.3.54.29: Thus instructed by Rāvaṇa, those rākṣasīs took hold of Maithilī and went to the aśoka grove.
t.3.54.28: There, all of you, with terrible threats and then again with soothing words, bring this Maithilī under your control, as one tames a wild she-elephant of the forest.
t.3.54.31: But she, Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, her limbs overcome with grief, fell into the power of the rākṣasīs, like a doe among tigresses.
t.3.54.30: It was surrounded by trees whose fruits granted every desire and that bore flowers and fruits of many kinds, and it was frequented by birds that were joyfully intoxicated in every season.
t.3.54.32: But there Maithilī found no peace, fiercely threatened by the women with hideous eyes; remembering her beloved husband and her brother-in-law, she fell senseless, tormented by fear and grief.
